messages.subject: Re: %*% (Vector dot or Matrix product)
parts:
Hi Mehmet,
Actually it does look a parser bug:

the symbol "%*%" seems to be parsed into the AST as "%42%" !

If you update the test to :

@Test
  public void matrixProduct() throws IOException{
    ExpressionVector result = parseAll("c(1,2,3) %*% c(7,8,7)\n");

FunctionCall call = (FunctionCall)result.getElementAsSEXP(0);
    
    assertThat(call.getFunction(), equalTo(symbol("%*%")); 
  }

This will give you a good basis for tracking down the bug.
Since 42 is the unicode point for the character *, there is probably a call somewhere to StringBuilder.append(int) instead of StringBuilder.appendCodePoint(int)

Best,

Alex

On Fri, Sep 9, 2011 at 2:34 PM, Mehmet Hakan Satman <mhsa...@gmail.com> wrote:
using backquotes do not help. The test

@Test
  public void matrixProduct() throws IOException{
    ExpressionVector result = parseAll("c(1,2,3) %*% c(7,8,7)\n");
    assertThat(result.toString(), equalTo(""));
  }

results as

got: expression(%42%(c(1,2,3), c(7,8,7)))

it seems it parses the function name and the parameters correctly but the problem is @Primitive("%*%") cannot be found at runtime.

confused..

Great!
Thanks for cleaning up my errors in the parser!

For the matrix operations, take a look at apache commons math / lapack - i'm not sure but I believe we can get most of the matrix operations "for free". I've added lapack to the project this weekend and experimented with the commons math api but I think I did something wrong with the adapter class becuase I could not get it to produce the correct results for a svd operation.

If there is functionality that commons doesn't provide, it may be worth pulling in another of the java math libraries, like colt. It would of course be nice to limit renjin's dependencies, but I think the benefits of reusing existing, well-tested code are more significant. 

I've written up some notes here: http://code.google.com/p/renjin/wiki/ThirdParty

As for models, yes, this is a big hairy chunk. Like many things in R, models like x ~ y are not actually part of the language per se, but are simply a set of related functions. the tilde operator (~) is just a binary function that constructs FunctionCall objects which store metadata information in certain attributes.

The C implementation of these functions (~, terms.formula, etc) is quite complex and somewhat inscrutable, I think this is a case where the best plan would be to do a literal port of the C, establish high test coverage, and then refactor at measure.

http://www.google.com/codesearch#ph23m5MVwzs/trunk/R-2.10.1-patched/src/main/model.c

Best,

Alex

messages.subject: Re: %*% (Vector dot or Matrix product)
parts:
Hi Alex,

With a little modification i made your commented SVD run with correct singular values. But the ambiguity starts with the wrong signs of U and V matrices.

It has been said that in "http://dsp.ucsd.edu/~kreutz/PEI-05%20Support%20Files/ECE275AB%20Lecture%209%20Viewgraphs%202008-2009.pdf":

"Obviously having access to the SVD is tremendously useful. With the background we
have now covered, one can now can greatly appreciate the utility of the Matlab
command svd(A) which returns the singular values, left singular vectors, and right
singular vectors of A, from which one can construct all of the entities described above.
(Note that the singular vectors returned by Matlab will not necessarily all agree with the
ones you construct by other means because of the ambiguites mentioned above.
However, the singular values will be the same, and the left and right singular vector
associated with the same, distinct singular value should only differ from yours by a sign
at most.) Another useful Matlab command is pinv(A) which returns the pseudoinverse of
A regardless of the value of the rank of A."


Unfortunately, there is considerable amount of literature about the sign ambiguity of singular values decomposition. Your current code seems good ve Lapack.xxx methods and using commons.math.svd requires more work. there is an algorithm for this ambiguity on "http://prod.sandia.gov/techlib/access-control.cgi/2007/076422.pdf" and googling it may result more.

all the best
